Proof: square roots s_n of p - 1/(n+1) on the universal cover; deck signs eps_n = (-1)^winding; over D_k the components of the preimage are exactly the 2^k sign classes of sigma_0..sigma_{k-1} (GX.cantZ_comp), the hard half realising every eventually constant sign pattern (eventual constancy: a loop stays away from 0, GX.cant_eps_eventually) by small circles around the 1/(n+1), n >= k, and the circle of radius R_k around 0, inside D_k; ends over 0 = sign sequences, a continuous bijection from the compact {0,1}^N onto the Hausdorff fibre.

l.1573: 'This answers positively Problem 10.7 of MR2198590' is bibliographic and not formalized; with the corrected Gamma_2' the example does exhibit a Cantor fibre over a point of the branching locus.
questions: Is the bibliographic sentence 'answers positively Problem 10.7 of MR2198590' (l.1573) outside the row's certification, as taken here (row closed under DEC-69)? If the master reads it as an assertion, downgrade to partial.

labels.label: ex:wild_cantor_general_antoine

hypotheses.paper: S a wild Cantor set [general_antoine] in S^3
hypotheses.note: DEC-58, DEC-68 (f), DEC-82: ONE explicit Antoine necklace GX.antoineNecklace, built and proved a Cantor set (GX.antoineNecklace_isCantorSubset) and proved WILD from the residual alone, sorry-free: GX.isWildCantor_antoineNecklace_of_res (no homeomorphism of S^3 carries it INTO a great circle) and GX.antoineNecklace_not_tame_of (none carries it ONTO the standard Cantor set GX.standardCantor3, itself proved a Cantor set on the great circle, GX.standardCantor3_isCantorSubset)

GX.IsWildCantor C := C Cantor and no homeomorphism of S^3 carries C into a great circle; this implies classical wildness (not ambiently homeomorphic to the standard Cantor set, GX.antoineNecklace_not_tame_of). The tame side is PROVED (no longer a named hypothesis): GX.tameCantorSLSC, the complement of any Cantor subset of a great circle is semi-locally simply connected in S^3, by general position (GX.gc_join, GX.gc_loop_null, GX.gc_paths_homotopicIn)

hypotheses.paper: (the conclusion) S^3 minus S not semi-locally simply connected in S^3
hypotheses.note: GX.antoineNecklace_wild_not_isSLSCInCC (literal, DEC-55, with the wildness) and GX.antoineNecklace_not_isSLSCIn(CC); derived SORRY-FREE from the single residual GX.AntoineMeridianEssentialTop (GX.antoineNecklace_wild_not_isSLSCInCC_of_top); the residual itself is the file's one sorry GX.antoineMeridianEssentialTop
DEC-55: literal and homotopy forms agree for closed C in S^3 (GX.sphere3_isSLSCInCC_compl_iff)

sorries.obstruction: Antoine's lemma proper, exactly GX.AntoineMeridianEssentialTop: for k >= 1 the meridian GX.antoineMeridian of the top link L is not null-homotopic in S^3 minus C_k (GX.antoineStage k, the 64^k linked square solid tori of generation k). Proved around it: every generation n < m reduces to this one by self-similarity (GX.antoineMeridianEssentialStrict_of_top: the inverse similarity GX.antoineCompInv conjugated by the stereographic chart extends continuously over the pole, GX.continuous_antoinePhi, and carries the complements correctly, GX.antoinePhi_mapsTo); the equal-generation case n = m is proved (GX.antoineMeridianEssential_self, the map GX.antoineTheta : S^3 minus L_{v,n} -> C minus 0 under which the meridian winds once). For k >= 1 no abelian invariant can detect it: the meridian disc of L meets exactly one link of the first chain, twice with opposite signs, so the meridian is null-homologous in S^3 minus C_k and every map to C minus 0 / every abelian covering kills it. A proof needs a non-abelian invariant valid for every k: Antoine's van Kampen computation for a closed chain of linked solid tori (pi_1-injectivity of the boundary tori), or an explicit self-similar non-abelian covering of S^3 minus C_k (a G-cocycle on an open cover of the solid torus minus its 64-link chain, boundary data closed under the substitution). mathlib has no van Kampen theorem, no pi_1 of a link complement and no covering built from a cocycle; building the 3-dimensional cocycle for the 64-link chain is the obstruction.

findings: Under DEC-58/DEC-68 (f) the example is about one explicit Antoine necklace, constructed, proved a Cantor set and (DEC-82) proved wild from the residual; the general wild-Cantor reading fails as soon as some wild Cantor set has simply connected, locally non-separating complement (GX.wild_cantor_claim_false_of_exists, proved).

l.1578: the conclusion does not depend on wildness; for the necklace it reduces (proved) to Antoine's lemma for the top link (GX.AntoineMeridianEssentialTop), at ONE point of S (the fixed point of g_0). Conversely wildness follows from the conclusion: the complement of a Cantor subset of a great circle (a tame Cantor set) IS semi-locally simply connected (GX.tameCantorSLSC, proved), so a Cantor set satisfying the conclusion is automatically wild.

kb_proposals: General position off a codimension-2 linear stratum in S^3 needs no transversality theory: approximate a loop by a polygon with hat functions (GX.gcHat, GX.gc_sum_hat), push each vertex off the plane in a direction transverse to the previous vertex's projection (GX.gcPick, GX.gcSeq: det(u, c + k u_perp) = det(u,c) + k|u|^2, two values of k cannot both fail), then cone off to a base point ON the stratum (GX.gc_loop_null).

A winding-number invariant of a solid-torus complement that extends over the pole of S^3: make it EVENTUALLY CONSTANT far out (GX.antoinePsi = (rho - 7/8) + i z with cut-offs), so continuity at infinity is local constancy, not a limit; choose it so that the meridian maps EXACTLY to r e^{2 pi i t}, giving an explicit exp-lift (GX.antoinePsi_meridian).

Self-similar Cantor constructions: extend an affine similarity of R^3 over the pole by bounding dist(f^{-1} p, 0) >= dist(p,0) - C from the contraction estimate of f (GX.antoineCompInv_dist_ge) and dist(stereo q, N)^2 = 4/(|q|^2+1) (GX.continuous_antoinePhi).
